lede: Columbus had last change, so Rick Bowness picked most of these matchups. Columbus played without Emil Andrae. Florida played without Radko Gudas.

notes.head: The fourth line drew Hathaway’s line
notes.text: Rick Bowness sent Heinen, Lomberg and Voronkov out for 5:06 of their 8:33 at 5-on-5 against Hathaway, Lafferty and Imama (60%, about 22% with no line matching), and they had the worse of the chances, 0.13 to 0.26 expected goals.

notes.head: Nichushkin’s line drew Reinhart’s line
notes.text: Monahan, Nichushkin and Garland spent 7:22 of their 11:21 at 5-on-5 against Eller, Verhaeghe and Reinhart (65%, about 28% with no line matching), and they had the better of the chances, 1.00 to 0.67 expected goals. Florida scored one of its seven goals then.

notes.head: The third line drew Bennett’s line
notes.text: Coyle, Olivier and Sillinger spent 5:47 of their 9:31 at 5-on-5 against Bennett, M. Tkachuk and B. Tkachuk (61%, about 24% with no line matching). Florida scored one of its seven goals then.

notes.head: One matchup paid off
notes.text: Johnson, Knies and Fantilli kept drawing Florida’s third line, Luostarinen, Lundell and Vilmanis. In those 5:58 Columbus had 0.40 expected goals to Florida’s 0.00. Columbus scored one of its three goals then.

foot: Rick Bowness matched harder than in his other home games: each line spent 57% of its time against one opposing line, against 37% to 47% in his first three.
